name: Slow Cooker Kalua Pork Bowls
intro_html: Kalua pork is Hawaiian comfort food at its simplest: pork, cabbage, and a long slow cook. This is a genuinely cheap bowl at just ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost), and it still delivers {{protein}} grams of protein. Fourteen servings from a short ingredient list is proof that good food does not have to be complicated.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt): ~$0.02. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $19.98 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.43 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $21.81 across 14 servings, roughly $1.56 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $2.76 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $24.57. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: This recipe wins on a short ingredient list. Just pork, rice, and cabbage means fewer things to buy and less to go wrong.
Green cabbage is one of the best deals in the produce aisle at under 70 cents a pound, and it cooks down soft and savory.
Season with plain salt and let the slow cooker do the rest. There is no need for fancy spice blends here.
make_it: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker, season it well with salt, and pour the liquid smoke over the top.
Add a splash of water, cover, and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours until it falls apart.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it through the juices.
Pile the chopped cabbage on top of the pork.
Cover and cook another 30 to 45 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Serve the pork and cabbage over cooked white rice and portion out.
portion_html: Every serving comes in around {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

upsell_html: Three ingredients, about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost), and it tastes like the islands. Hard to argue with that. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
